description:
Find long-form hooks: how the YouTube videos that beat their own channel open, on a
    topic. Long-form YouTube only, never Shorts, TikTok or Instagram (for those: find_hooks).

    What it does: searches YouTube for long-form videos on the topic, keeps only the
    outliers (a video whose views are at least min_outlier times the median views of its
    own channel's recent uploads; 2 by default) posted in 2023 or later (nothing older is
    ever delivered), reads the first intro_seconds (60 by default) of each one's
    transcript, and says why that opening holds a viewer.

    What comes back: the run's `finds`, ranked, strongest outlier first. Each has title,
    channel, watch_url, player_url (an iframe src), thumbnail_url, views,
    channel_median_views, outlier (28.2 means 28 times the channel's usual), outlier_score
    (0 to 100 on one fixed scale: nothing else a run found moves it, so finds from
    different runs rank together), outlier_tier, channel_size, likes_per_1k, posted_at,
    duration_s, and the opening: intro (the first minute as it was said: lines of n, t in
    seconds, text) and intro_text, always whole; and inside it the hook (verbatim: the lines
    the analysis marks as the hook, ending on a sentence end, at most 25 seconds and 60
    words, with hook_words, hook_start_s and hook_end_s, a sponsor read or greeting at the
    front left out; hook_seconds is hook_end_s). auto_captions says the opening has almost
    no punctuation. about_subject is yes or partly: a video the model judges not to be
    about the subject is dropped. The analysis: hook_type (the same list as find_hooks),
    mechanism (why it holds, quoting the opening word for word), promise, open_loop,
    title_link (how the first lines pay off the title), beats (the opening in parts: from,
    to, beat, does),
    opens_with (cold_open, greeting, teaser, question, sponsor), format (the kind of
    video), angle, template (the hook as a fill-in structure), steal_it and audience. When
    the topic asks for a kind of opening ("question hooks", "storytime"), style_match says
    whether each find is that kind and the matches come first. analysed is false
    when the model could not analyse an opening: the opening is still real, its analysis
    fields are null. The run's report.patterns lists the opening types at least two finds
    share; report.shape says how the openings are built, counted from the finds
    (hook_seconds, how long the hook runs, and hook_words as medians, beats with how many
    openings use each and the second it usually starts_at, and the sequence of beats most
    of them share); and
    report.openers holds up to `openers` (3 by default, 0 for none) openings WRITTEN for
    your topic from those structures (hook, then, hook_type, based_on). report.openers_label
    is always "Written by Hook Detector from the structure of these real openings": show
    it with them, never present one as a real video's opening. report.landscape is the
    subject at a glance, counted from the videos the run held against their own channel
    (videos, channels, outliers and their share, breakouts, small_channel_outliers,
    recent_outliers). The run's hooks and bonus are always empty.

    A link instead of a subject: when topic is a channel's YouTube address
    (https://www.youtube.com/@name, or just @name) the run returns that channel's OWN
    outliers, its recent long-form uploads that beat its usual (one provider call, no
    search); when it is a long-form video's address the run returns that one video,
    whatever its multiple (requested is 1). options.link says "channel" or "video". No
    openings are written for a link (use remix_find on a find to write for your niche).
    A Short's address is refused with 422.

    Arguments: topic 3 to 500 characters; count 1 to 30 (default 8); language and country
    optional; posted_within_days 30, 90, 365 or 730 to narrow the 2023 floor further;
    channel_size "small", "medium" or "large" to keep only channels of that size (by what
    their uploads usually get), so a small creator sees breakouts from channels their own
    size; reuse=true (default) starts from the videos your last long or packaging run on
    this topic bought within a week, and a video you already had read is delivered from
    that read (analysis_from_earlier_read) at no model or provider cost. seen_before says
    an earlier run of yours already found the video. idempotency_key: always pass one and
    reuse it on a retry. wait_seconds 0 to 50: 0 returns the run_id at once; above 0 waits
    and returns the run. Starts are limited per account per hour (429 rate_limited).

    Cost: reserves up to 90 credits for 20 videos or fewer and 5 more for each video above
    that (140 at 30; less on a smaller balance, down to 25) and charges
    only the provider calls it made: the searches, one call per channel measured, one per
    transcript read. A failed run costs nothing, and so does a run that
    finds nothing, inside the same allowance a hook run has (the outcome says so).

    Timing and next step: how long a run takes has not been measured yet, so never assume
    a time. Call get_run with wait_seconds=50 until status is done or failed;
    progress.items holds the finds written so far as cards
    and progress.scan the videos it is looking at while it runs. Then keep_find, export_run. Same as POST /v1/longform. Needs the research
    permission (403 insufficient_scope otherwise).

channel_size.description: optional: only videos from channels of this size, by what the channel's uploads usually get (its median views, the figure the outlier is measured against): small (under 20,000), medium (up to 200,000) or large. Null or left out: any size
channel_size.title: Channel Size

count.description: how many long-form hooks to deliver, 1 to 30
count.title: Count

country.description: optional, an assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (US, GB, MA): searches YouTube as seen from this country. It steers the search; it does not filter the channels
country.title: Country

idempotency_key.description: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters; the same key within 24 hours returns the first run instead of paying for a second
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

intro_seconds.description: optional, 20 to 120 (default 60): how many seconds of each video's opening to read and return
intro_seconds.title: Intro Seconds

language.description: optional, up to 60 characters: the language the videos should be spoken in, in words or as a tag ("Spanish", "pt-BR"). Left out, it is read from the topic's own language
language.title: Language

min_outlier.description: optional, 1.5 to 100 (default 2): how many times its own channel's usual views a video must have to count as an outlier. Only outliers are ever delivered
min_outlier.title: Min Outlier

openers.description: optional, 0 to 6 (default 3): how many openings to write for the subject from the structure of the real ones; 0 for none
openers.title: Openers

posted_within_days.description: optional, how recent the videos must be, as days: 30, 90, 365, 730. Null or left out means everything since 2023-01-01; nothing older is ever delivered
posted_within_days.title: Posted Within Days

reuse.description: start from the videos your last long or packaging run on this topic already bought (within a week), so the second tab on a topic costs little
reuse.title: Reuse

topic.description: the subject to research, 3 to 500 characters, in any language. Or a YouTube address instead of a subject: a channel's (https://www.youtube.com/@name, or just @name) returns that channel's own outliers, its recent long-form uploads that beat its usual; a long-form video's (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...) returns that one video, whatever its multiple. A Short's address is refused (422)
topic.title: Topic

wait_seconds.description: 0 to 50: seconds to wait for the run to finish; 0 returns at once
wait_seconds.title: Wait Seconds

name: find_long_hooks
